Latest Update: So you got a Microsoft Voluntary Exit Offer? Here’s what to do next

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1416 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.
  • Nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn.
  • Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a massive decision to make in the next few weeks: take the manufacturer’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.

Nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn. This is the fourth post in his series on “Life after Substantial Tech,” including the Seattle startup guide, laid off at 50 and VC funding is changing dramatically.

Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a massive decision to make in the next few weeks: take the manufacturer’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.

According to recent reports, microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman revealed the initiative in a memo on Oct. 26: a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) for about 60,000 employees at level 70 and below, which includes general managers and some vice presidents, in the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and India. That’s roughly 27% of Microsoft’s 223,000 people. The company expects 3,000 or fewer of them to accept.

Microsoft notes the terms match its standard severance: base pay tied to level and tenure, continued stock vesting, a period of health coverage and career transition help. The severance package varies greatly based on the seniority or level of the employee and the number of years of service. Employees have until early December to decide and would leave by the end of the year.

The offer follows the Voluntary Retirement Program (VRP) that Microsoft extended to about 8,750 U.S. employees in April. About 30% of them, or roughly 2,600 people, took that offer.

All of this comes as Microsoft cuts jobs and changes the kinds of roles it hires for, while pouring money into AI infrastructure and data centers. At the same time, AI is reshaping the broader workforce, flattening management layers and changing what employers look for in newly introduced hires.

Industry observers note that the worry I hear most is whether more layoffs are waiting on the other side. So the real choice is whether you leave on your own terms or let the tech giant decide for you.

I hear two questions from Microsoft employees thinking about the VEO: How easily can I get another job, and how hard is it to start a company right now?

Harder than you think, and it depends a lot on who you are. We are in the “low hire, low fire” economy.

It has been revealed that there is MASSIVE demand for AI-native builders — product managers, data scientists and engineers — as companies adapt products to deal with AI. Companies are also in the process of adopting AI.

One of the fastest-growing tech roles is the “Forward Deployed Engineer,” who implements AI solutions at customers. Security is also job #1 as models and agents get smarter and better at hacking legacy systems.

But it is very hard to be seen by recruiters and hiring managers right now. Candidates are using AI to customize their resumes to each job and using AI agents to apply, sending out 100 to 200 job applications per day. Recruiters are inundated with resumes and job applications, many of which are fake or inappropriate for the role.

It is critical to leverage your network in the job search, which can be hard if you have spent your entire career within one firm.

It has been revealed that hiring managers have changed what they look for, too. AI fluency is becoming table stakes. The “process” of how you build/sell/market with AI is more important than what you build. Candidates are expected to show prototypes and proof of how they use AI tools every day.

In a recent development, the jobs themselves are changing. A friend told me last month that he wanted an engineering manager role. There are fewer manager roles in the market now.

In a recent development, AI has driven a reduction in management layers and a general flattening of organizations. The engineering team at a small AI manufacturer today is a CTO and a group of strong individual contributors. It is normal for managers to have 10 to 30 direct reports now, versus five to 10 in the pre-AI era.

Product management, program management and design teams are shrinking, as well, as AI automates certain jobs.

Industry observers note that hiring managers may view spending your whole career at Microsoft as a yellow flag. Microsoft is an iconic but unusual company. Almost no one else sells to and services customers the way Microsoft does, with an account executive inside nearly every large enterprise in the world.

The skills that get you promoted in Redmond don’t always carry over to a 500- to 5,000-person software tech giant.

It has never been easier to build a product, and it has rarely been harder to fund a company.

Software is cheap to build now. A product leader and an engineer using AI tools can ship in weeks what used to take a team a year.

In a recent development, this cuts both ways for startups. Every good idea attracts a dozen competitors within months, and the big platforms will copy anything that works.

In a recent development, the true strength of a startup today is the ability to grow revenue rapidly and establish leadership in a beachhead market. The sales, marketing, product-led growth and distribution strategies are becoming the most critical parts of the business.

The bar for venture funding is extremely high. Jason Lemkin of SaaStr recently shared data from ICONIQ showing that top “AI forward” startups under $10 million in annual recurring revenue are growing 900% a year at the median.

One venture investor told me they advise their portfolio companies that if they aren’t on track for a $10 million run rate within two years, they won’t raise another round. Last week I spoke with an investor who owns part of a business with $4 million in revenue, growing 100% a year and losing $1 million, and it can’t raise.

There are three fundraising paths.

Sources indicate that 1) Think VERY substantial, raise a lot and grow fast enough to justify it. Build an incredible team pursuing an ambitious idea. Raise a large round based on the promise of becoming the next Anthropic, OpenAI or legal AI startup Harvey. Many of the most interesting companies are not software or AI-related, but are “deep tech” companies in defense, robotics, energy and biotech.

It has been revealed that 2) Raise a moderate amount of money from angels, family offices and nontraditional funds to build a business that has the ability to be profitable on one round of financing. You can control your destiny by building a company that doesn’t rely on the venture capital funding market.

According to recent reports, 3) Bootstrap and build a business that you own. Fund it yourself, grow it with revenue and get to profitability.

The question that most people are NOT asking is: What do I really want?

Before December, block out an afternoon and think about the last time you were happy at work.

There are many frameworks for figuring out what you want in your career and life in general. I’m a fan of the Four Elements exercise. Write down three times in your career when you felt energized and effective. From those, work out what gives you energy, where you have the most impact, what culture you do best in and what your constraints are: money, kids, aging parents and how many more years you want to work.

On LinkedIn, I have seen examples of Microsoft employees taking the VEO to start their own businesses in property management, buy car washes, take time to recharge, spend time with family and travel.

Recent findings suggest that other employees are starting the job search in earnest but not taking the VEO. Many others are just getting back to work and doubling down on Microsoft.

According to recent reports, whichever way you go, start now. Start by aligning on your priorities and what you want from your career. If you stay, use the next year to build your skills with AI and to grow a network outside Redmond. If you leave to build something, decide early which of the three funding paths you’re on, because that choice shapes everything that follows.

The people I’ve watched land well after Big Tech had one thing in common: they knew what they wanted before they walked out the door, whether that was a new role, a tech giant of their own or a year with their family.

Our Mainland China operations are organized into three reportable segments: mainland China public securities, mainland China asset management, and mainland China insurance. Each segment operates under a dedicated brand and serves a distinct client need in the mainland China market.

Mainland China public securities.

Mainland China public securities, operating under the Noah Upright brand, is the business that distributes mutual funds and private secondary products in mainland China. This segment operates under an "online-first, offline-supported" business model, with the goal of facilitating global asset allocation through RMB-denominated products.

Mainland China asset management.

Mainland China asset management, operating under the Gopher Asset Management brand, is the business that manages RMB-denominated private equity funds and private secondary products. Current focus areas include managing primary market exits on existing vintages and growing cross-border ETF products in the secondary market.

It has been revealed that mainland China insurance, operating under the Glory brand, is the business that distributes insurance products in mainland China, consisting mainly of life and health insurance products. The business has been undergoing a strategic shift toward a commission-only broker model and comprehensive family succession planning services. The net revenues for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB1.3 million (US$0.2 million).

Our international operations are organized into three reportable segments: international wealth management, international asset management, and international insurance and comprehensive services. The Manufacturer operates booking centers in Hong Kong, Singapore and key U.S. markets including Upcoming York, Los Angeles and Silicon Valley.

International wealth management.

Industry observers note that international wealth management, operating under the ARK Wealth Management brand, is the business that provides offline and online wealth management services to global Chinese high-net-worth investors outside mainland China. At the moment we are dedicated to providing comprehensive services using our booking centers in Hong Kong and Singapore.

International asset management, operating under the Olive Asset Management brand, is the business that manages USD-denominated private equity funds and private secondary products, with a dedicated U.S. product center and partnerships with top-tier global managers across structured products and hedge funds. We are building our offices in Hong Kong, Singapore, Japan and key U.S. markets, including Newly introduced York and Silicon Valley.

International insurance and comprehensive services.

International insurance and comprehensive services, operating under the Glory Family Heritage brand, is the business that provides comprehensive international services such as insurance distribution, trust services and other family office-style services. With offices in Hong Kong, Singapore and Los Angeles, we provide global coverage to clients.

Headquarters reflects revenue generated from corporate operations at the Firm's headquarters in Singapore and office in Shanghai, as well as administrative costs and expenses that are not directly allocated to the aforementioned six business segments, including investments in platform-wide technology, AI infrastructure and corporate functions.

In a recent development, "In the third quarter of 2026, global markets became more volatile, and many high-net-worth clients shifted toward caution, liquidity and diversification," commented Ms. Jingbo Wang, Co-founder and Chairwoman of Noah. "We used this period to reposition the business. We stayed with our decision to step back from insurance distribution and put our resources into investment products and global asset allocation, where our long-term strengths lie. Even as markets pulled back, demand for our investment products held up, and our overseas business continued to deliver steady contributions.".

"This quarter's results also include several one-off costs from streamlining our organization. We see these as investments in a leaner, more focused Noah.".

"Building on the foundation we set out in the first half of the year, our use of AI is enhancing both the quality of our client service and the efficiency of our organization. It allows our relationship managers to serve more clients with greater consistency and helps our four global booking centers work together more seamlessly. Looking ahead, we will keep strengthening our global platform, risk management and technology capabilities to create long-term value for our clients and shareholders.".

THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS.

Net revenues for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB509.0 million (US$75.9 million), a 19.6% decrease from the corresponding period in 2025, primarily due to lower one-time commissions from international insurance distribution and lower recurring service fees from mainland China private equity products, partially offset by higher performance-based income from mainland China private secondary products.

These are changes in segment names only and do not involve any material change in the nature or scope of the underlying business activities included in the respective segments. Accordingly, the financial and operating information presented under the renamed segments remains comparable to the corresponding information previously presented under the former segment names.

It has been revealed that operating costs and expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB445.1 million (US$66.4 million), a 3.5% decrease from the corresponding period in 2025. Operating costs and expenses for the third quarter of 2026 primarily consisted of (i) compensation and benefits of RMB270.0 million (US$40.3 million); (ii) selling expenses of RMB54.1 million (US$8.1 million); (iii) general and administrative expenses of RMB87.4 million (US$13.0 million); (iv) provision for credit losses of RMB2.9 million (US$0.4 million); (v) other operating expenses of RMB31.0 million (US$4.6 million); less (vi) income from government subsidies of RMB0.3 million (US$0.05 million).

Operating margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 12.6%, compared with 27.2% for the corresponding period in 2025.

Interest income for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB29.5 million (US$4.4 million), a 2.8% increase from the corresponding period in 2025.

Investment income for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB85.5 million (US$12.7 million), compared with RMB20.6 million in the corresponding period in 2025, primarily due to higher fair value gains on investments held by consolidated funds.

Income tax expense for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB62.1 million (US$9.3 million), an 8.0% decrease from the corresponding period in 2025.

Non-GAAP Net Income Attributable to Noah Shareholders.

As of September 30, 2026, the Firm had RMB3,891.7 million (US$580.5 million) in cash and cash equivalents, compared with RMB4,322.7 million as of June 30, 2026 and RMB3,837.4 million as of September 30, 2025.

Industry observers note that net cash inflow from the Company's operating activities during the third quarter of 2026 was RMB175.0 million (US$26.1 million), compared with a net cash inflow of RMB316.9 million in the corresponding period in 2025. The decrease was primarily due to lower income from operations and decreases in contingent liabilities.

In a recent development, net cash inflow from the Manufacturer's investing activities during the third quarter of 2026 was RMB32.3 million (US$4.8 million), compared with a net cash inflow of RMB253.7 million in the corresponding period in 2025. The decrease was primarily due to lower net proceeds from redemptions of held-to-maturity investments.

Net cash outflow from the Company's financing activities during the third quarter of 2026 was RMB612.0 million (US$91.3 million), compared with a net cash outflow of RMB549.9 million in the corresponding period in 2025, primarily due to higher dividend payments.

According to recent reports, noah Holdings Limited (NYSE: NOAH and HKEX: 6686) is a leading and pioneer wealth management service provider offering comprehensive one-stop advisory services on global investment and asset allocation primarily for global Chinese high-net-worth investors. Noah's American depositary shares, or ADSs, are listed on the Newly introduced York Stock Exchange under the symbol "NOAH," and its shares are listed on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under the stock code "6686." One ADS represents five ordinary shares, par value $0.00005 per share.

In the first nine months of 2026, Noah distributed RMB56.5 billion (US$8.4 billion) of investment products. Through Gopher Asset Management and Olive Asset Management, Noah had assets under management of RMB139.9 billion (US$20.9 billion) as of September 30, 2026.

Founded in 2005, the firm pioneered a business model combining wealth management and asset management and has continued to build its international platform over the years. As of September 30, 2026, Noah had 470,522 registered clients. The Company reports its operations under six business segments â Mainland China public securities (Noah Upright), Mainland China asset management (Gopher Asset Management), Mainland China insurance (Glory), International wealth management (ARK Wealth Management), International asset management (Olive Asset Management), and International insurance and comprehensive services (Glory Family Heritage) â plus headquarters. As of September 30, 2026, Noah had established branches and service capabilities across mainland China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Japan, and key U.S. markets, including Newly introduced York, Los Angeles, and Silicon Valley, and has been expanding into markets such as Canada, Australia, and the United Kingdom, reflecting its international operating footprint.

For more information, please visit Noah's investor relations website at ir.noahgroup.com.

As of Nov. 20, Shiba Inu (SHIB) is about $10 million in market capitalization short of overtaking Bittensor (TAO) for the No. 33 spot in CoinMarketCap's global crypto ranking. TAO has a market cap of $2.18 billion at a price of $186.41, and SHIB has $2.17 billion at $0.000003691 and ranks No. 34.

A gain of about 0.5% in SHIB's price, with TAO's price unchanged, would be enough for the meme coin to take Bittensor's place in the ranking.

According to recent reports, TAO is the token of the Bittensor AI network, and Digital Currency Group (DCG) founder Barry Silbert has been one of its most vocal backers. Silbert also runs Yuma, a DCG company that builds on Bittensor.

At Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference in September 2025, Silbert said that Bittensor was the thing he had gotten most excited about since Bitcoin. "I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence.".

On Dec. 30, 2025, DCG's Grayscale filed with the SEC to convert its Grayscale Bittensor Trust into a spot exchange-traded fund on NYSE Arca under the ticker GTAO. The filing came after Bittensor's first halving in mid-December 2025, and at the end of that month, TAO was trading at about $222. "We're pleased to take this early step as we continue to expand the tools available to investors," a Grayscale spokesperson said.

The gap between the two tokens closed because TAO fell. TAO was one of the market's strongest tokens this year. In April, the token was up 55% since January, and in October it rallied again and was up 43% for the year, according to TradingView data.

Industry observers note that the November correction erased those gains. On Nov. 20, TAO was trading 16.95% below its January level, and it lost 12.16% over the past week.

It has been revealed that SHIB spent most of the year in the red. The meme coin rose about 25% in January, and it has not been in positive territory since February. By Nov. 20, SHIB had lost about 50% since the start of the year, and it fell 13.79% over the past week.

Sources indicate that TAO had a 24-hour trading volume of $172.19 million on Nov. 20, and SHIB had $55.17 million, according to CoinMarketCap data. TAO has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens, the same as Bitcoin's, and SHIB has about 589 trillion tokens in circulation.

It has been revealed that shiba Inu developer Mazrael responded to the drop on X on Nov. 17. "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB," he wrote in reply to a user who pointed to the falling price.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:51 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:51 pm.
  • Amazon and Newly introduced York City are fighting again.
  • It has been revealed that the Seattle tech giant is threatening to move its delivery operations out of the city over a proposed law that would require it to directly employ the drivers who bring packages to Newly introduced Yorkers’ doors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:51 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:51 pm.

Amazon and Newly introduced York City are fighting again.

It has been revealed that the Seattle tech giant is threatening to move its delivery operations out of the city over a proposed law that would require it to directly employ the drivers who bring packages to Newly introduced Yorkers’ doors. It’s also asking its customers to help fight the bill.

The legislation, known as the Delivery Protection Act or Intro 518, would apply to companies that run last-mile delivery facilities in the city. Amazon is the main target, but FedEx and several regional couriers would also be covered.

According to recent reports, companies would need a license from the city’s Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, which would also investigate complaints. The bill was introduced in February.

According to recent reports, on Thursday, Amazon began showing New York City customers pop-up messages and a homepage banner that reads, “NYC Council could add up to $5 per order. Act now to protect low prices.” The notices link to a form and a pre-written letter customers can send to their council members to oppose the bill, Bloomberg reported. Amazon pointed GeekWire to a study by consulting firm AKRF estimating the bill would raise consumer costs by $409 to $664 a year, but didn’t detail how it arrived at the per-order figure.

It has been revealed that in a blog post, Amazon noted it relies on a network of small delivery businesses in the city. “If this legislation passes, we’d no longer be able to work with them, and we’d be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city,” the company wrote. “That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.”.

According to recent reports, amazon released its Delivery Service Partners program in 2018, letting entrepreneurs start their own companies to deliver Amazon packages in Amazon-branded vans and uniforms. The companies hire their own drivers, while Amazon pays them to deliver and offers discounts on vehicles, fuel and insurance. The model lets Amazon expand its delivery network without directly employing drivers.

Recent findings suggest that in a statement to GeekWire, Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel stated the bill “as written” would threaten more than 40 small delivery businesses the company works with in the city and the more than 5,000 New Yorkers they employ. More than 2,000 Amazon employees also work at its delivery facilities in the city, the company said.

“We’re hopeful this bill doesn’t pass as written,” Nantel said. “But so far, key City Council members seem uninterested in learning about our delivery operations.” Amazon said neither Council Member Tiffany Cabán, the bill’s sponsor, nor Mayor Zohran Mamdani has accepted its offer to visit a delivery facility. The manufacturer also said customers sent about 20,000 emails to council members within six hours of the campaign’s launch Thursday morning.

Recent findings suggest that the standoff echoes Amazon’s 2019 reversal on its second headquarters. That February, the manufacturer abruptly canceled looks to build a 25,000-person “HQ2” office in Long Island City, Queens, after more than a year of competition among cities to host it. Amazon blamed “a number of state and local politicians” who opposed the project, which drew fierce criticism over roughly $3 billion in government incentives.

In a recent development, amazon stuck with its prepares for Arlington, Va., and Nashville and didn’t reopen its search. Polls at the time indicated most Fresh Yorkers supported the deal, but Queens officials, labor leaders and activists fought it. State Sen. Michael Gianaris, who led the opposition, accused Amazon of trying to shake down governments to get its way.

It defies logic that Amazon, a $3 trillion corporation, would raise Upcoming Yorkers’ cost of living if it’s forced to adhere to basic regulations and worker protections.We are crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs.If… https://t.co/UWXVTJhRL6.

City leaders backing the delivery bill see a familiar pattern. “Amazon is once again making spurious attacks against this commonsense legislation that would make workers and our streets safer,” stated Cabán, the bill’s sponsor, who called Amazon’s warning a “dishonest scare tactic.”.

City Council Speaker Julie Menin questioned Amazon’s cost claims in a post on X.

“It defies logic that Amazon, a $3 trillion corporation, would raise Newly introduced Yorkers’ cost of living if it’s forced to adhere to basic regulations and worker protections,” she wrote, adding that the council is “crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs.”.

Mamdani endorsed the bill in August, saying Amazon’s subcontractor model “leaves workers vulnerable and corporations free to avoid accountability for reckless conditions on city streets,” CNBC reported.

Supporters, including the Teamsters union, which has sought to organize Amazon drivers and warehouse workers, say the bill would make the work safer and make it harder for Amazon to distance itself from driver injuries.

It has been revealed that amazon disputes that the bill would improve safety. The company remarked it has invested more than $2.5 billion in driver safety since 2019, that the serious crash rate for its drivers in Fresh York City fell 35.7% from 2024 to 2025, and that drivers there have averaged nearly $24 an hour since January 2025, with required health coverage and paid time off.

Meanwhile, business groups have run ads against the bill and warned they may sue the city if it passes, according to CNBC. The measure is awaiting review by Menin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 12:19 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Sources indicate that cloudera Inc. today confirmed a digital sovereignty package that it said enables organizations to maintain control over their data, artificial intelligence models and computing infrastructure regardless of where workloads run.

Recent findings suggest that cloudera for Digital Sovereignty combines the company’s Anywhere Cloud, Open Data Lakehouse and Unified Data Fabric technologies with open-weight AI models and model customization tools from Mistral AI SAS, with whom Cloudera recently partnered. The integrated offering supports deployment across sovereign clouds, private data centers and fully air-gapped environments that have no connection to external networks.

In a recent development, digital sovereignty is becoming a more pressing glitch as enterprises move beyond managing data residency to ensuring that the AI models and infrastructure they depend upon remain under their control. McKinsey & Co. reported last year that 71% of the executives it surveyed called sovereign AI an “existential concern” or “strategic imperative.” Cloudera said its own research found that regulation, privacy and data sovereignty requirements rank among the top three barriers to scaling AI.

“As AI becomes more autonomous and embedded in critical operations, enterprises need to know that their data, models, and infrastructure can remain under their control even as technology and regulatory requirements change,” Cloudera Chief Technology Officer Sergio Gago said in a statement.

It has been revealed that the offering provides consistent zero-trust access controls, data lineage tracking and governance policies across deployment environments. Those capabilities are intended to help organizations address requirements imposed by the European Union’s AI Act, Digital Operational Resilience Act and Network and Information Security Directive, among other regulations.

It has been revealed that governance policies also extend to the enterprise data that AI agents retrieve and use in performing tasks. Mistral’s open-weight models can run alongside governed data, enabling organizations to customize models locally and execute agentic workflows without exposing sensitive information.

In a recent development, cloudera’s modular hybrid cloud architecture enables people to shift computing workloads between infrastructure providers and private data centers without rewriting applications or migrating or duplicating underlying data. Organizations can also selectively apply sovereignty controls to sensitive workloads without imposing the same restrictions across their entire computing estate.

Moor Insights & Strategy Inc. Chief Analyst Patrick Moorhead said AI has raised the bar on data protection. “A firm can meet every line of its sovereignty policy and still not control who accesses its data or who can turn off the models it depends on,” he said in a statement.

It has been revealed that cloudera noted it will supplement its Mistral partnership with an ecosystem of sovereign cloud providers and implementation partners. The company is initially targeting Europe but aims to expand the partner network into other regions and regulatory jurisdictions.

As cities act to shred housing’s red-tape, Boston homes in on parking

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (976 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that boston is an expensive place to build housing, and it is one of the priciest places in the country to live.
  • In a recent development, cutting parking is one path cities are taking to lower construction costs.
  • It has been revealed that boulder, Colorado, set a 90-day deadline for deciding affordable housing applications.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that boston is an expensive place to build housing, and it is one of the priciest places in the country to live. Its City Council has taken a step toward scrapping one costly requirement: parking.

In a recent development, cutting parking is one path cities are taking to lower construction costs. Others are chasing review time, density and tax incentives, and the changes are landing at the city and county level.

It has been revealed that boulder, Colorado, set a 90-day deadline for deciding affordable housing applications. Allentown, Pennsylvania, tied a tax break to affordable units. Lake County, Illinois, outside Chicago, opened all its residential zones to accessory dwelling units.

These local moves come as states test how far they can push cities to build in the name of approving housing affordability. California, Texas and Florida have passed laws that override local zoning authority. Lawmakers there have had to keep tightening them to head off workarounds.

Sources indicate that illinois and North Carolina may be next. Gov. J.B. Pritzker’s housing reform plan, which stalled this year, is expected to return in January.

A shift in political winds in the Tar Heel State may mean lawmakers try once again to pass broad reform after failing multiple times. But they did eliminate off-street parking requirements across most of the state.

More than 120 cities have eliminated parking mandates, according to the Parking Reform Network, an advocacy coalition.

According to recent reports, boston could be next. The city’s average asking rent was $3,065 a month in the third quarter, the fifth highest of the 90 markets Cushman & Wakefield tracks, behind San Francisco, Latest York, San Jose and Long Island. Home construction fell by 14,000 units between 2024-2025 and 2025-2026, according to this year’s Greater Boston Housing Report Card.

It has been revealed that the council voted 9-4 on Nov. 18 to remove parking requirements for new residential construction. The zoning commission must now approve the measure before it goes to the mayor.

Abundant Housing Massachusetts, the Commercial Real Estate Development Association, the Greater Boston Real Estate Board and the Environmental League of Massachusetts Action Fund support the measure.

Industry observers note that five years ago, Mayor Michelle Wu signed off on a zoning amendment to remove off-street parking requirements for affordable housing. Wu, who has championed zoning reform, hasn’t stated whether she supports the current measure.

“We will evaluate the implications of eliminating parking minimums citywide,” spokesperson Marcela Dwork noted in a statement.

Boston’s transportation department notes a garage space can cost up to $50,000, but the Pioneer Institute put underground spaces in Boston at $106,000 to $152,000 in late 2025.

Opponents argue the policy leaves out residents who need cars. But real estate professionals in Boston and elsewhere in the country note that such changes don’t mean parking vanishes.

“It’s about letting each Boston project respond to real demand, not one-size-fits-all formulas,” Reginald Jones-Booker, a Berkshire Hathaway agent, wrote on LinkedIn. “Developers can still include parking where it makes sense, but the mandate would no longer force every upcoming home to meet a fixed minimum.”.

Boulder’s council unanimously approved an ordinance on Nov. 19 that sets a 90-day decision deadline for complete applications. It applies to projects in which at least half the homes are affordable to low- and middle-income households.

Recent findings suggest that site reviews there have taken a median of 277 days over the past two years, according to Boulder Reporting Lab. Staff, not the Planning Board, will decide requests for extra height or reduced open space, and neighbors can appeal.

Sources indicate that the rules take effect Dec. 19. They are meant to keep Boulder eligible for Proposition 123, a 2022 voter-approved measure that sends state income tax revenue to affordable housing in cities that commit to growing their affordable stock by 3% a year.

According to recent reports, billy Joel’s 1982 hit “Allentown” made the Lehigh Valley city a symbol of a fading industrial America. Bethlehem Steel, the region’s anchor, ended most steelmaking in 1995 and was dissolved in 2003.

Those days are long gone, but the city now faces a different problem: keeping housing within reach as the region grows.

The City Council voted unanimously Nov. 18 to pass a workforce housing ordinance. Developers of projects with 10 or more units who receive a tax break under the Local Economic Revitalization Tax Assistance Act, a 1977 Pennsylvania law known as LERTA, must make at least 20% of the units affordable. Those units are rent-restricted for households earning 60% to 120% of area median income.

The city has no LERTA zone yet, so a council member said the amended version “does not directly impact workforce housing today.”.

Lake County amended its Unified Development Ordinance on Nov. 10, effective that day, to allow accessory dwelling units in all county residential zones. It also lowers their minimum lot sizes, adds incentives for conservation developments and creates an “early assistance” process for developers. The rules reach only unincorporated areas.

In a recent development, the county acted while the state stalled. Gov. J.B. Pritzker’s Building Up Illinois Developments plan, known as BUILD, would have legalized accessory dwelling units statewide, allowed missing-middle housing, set permit-review deadlines, ended excessive parking minimums and standardized impact fees.

It failed to advance before the spring session ended, after the Illinois Municipal League and suburban mayors objected to its zoning mandates. Pritzker has noted the blueprint will likely wait until January.

After Pritzker’s initiative stalled, Illinois REALTORS revived its Illinois Housing Supply Accelerator Program, launched in August. The program asks local officials to form working groups targeting barriers to building.

Pritzker said in October that he expected BUILD to wait until the full session starting in January. Lawmakers finished the first week of the fall veto session without major housing action. They return Dec. 1-3.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Alan Boyle on Nov 19, 2026 at 6:33 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 6:33 pm.

Redmond, Wash.-based RBC Signals has announced a $10 million strategic growth investment aimed at accelerating the tech giant’s expansion into government satellite data services and the commercialization of emerging space technologies.

RBC Signals supports satellite operators by arranging access to a global network of ground stations, including its own assets and antenna facilities operated by partners.

In August, for example, Blue Origin and RBC Signals confirmed a partnership to build out the ground infrastructure for Blue Origin’s Quartz communications network. RBC Signals is also a provider for the U.S. Space Force’s Joint Antenna Marketplace.

According to recent reports, the newly announced investment was led by Washington Harbour Partners, a private investment firm based in Washington, D.C. The firm ranked sixth among all defense technology investors in the Silicon Valley Defense Group’s 2026 NatSec100 Report.

“Our vision has always been to build a global, secure network of networks that makes space connectivity more accessible, flexible and reliable,” Ron Faith, RBC Signals’ president and CEO, said today in a news release.

“By bringing together infrastructure, partners and emerging technologies, we’re creating a dual-use platform that can evolve alongside the needs of the national defense and the commercial space industry,” Faith remarked. “This investment from Washington Harbour Partners will help us accelerate that vision by expanding our government services business and bringing emerging capabilities such as higher frequency bands, optical connectivity, intersatellite links and space domain awareness to market.”.

Recent findings suggest that mina Faltas, founder and CEO of Washington Harbour Partners, highlighted RBC Signals’ role in addressing the growing demand for space connectivity. “We see tremendous potential in the tech giant’s ability to deliver mission-critical capabilities, and we’re excited to support the team as they enter this next phase of growth,” Faltas said.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility.
  • According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is at the moment facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.
  • According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility. However, recent onchain data has shown an unexpected trend in exchange activity.

According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is at the moment facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.

According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.

Notably, the data further reveals that the metric has surpassed the previous reading of 2.09 recorded on July 6, marking a five-month high in XRP’s supply shortage index.

It is key to note that readings above +2 are a strong indication of severely tightened supply, which means that the amount of XRP available on the exchange has decreased significantly.

While negative readings often mean the opposite, this means that XRP has witnessed a sharp reversal from the supply level seen on September 27.

According to recent reports, at the time, the index stood at -1.5 while XRP traded above $1.50, signaling an abundance of XRP on Binance. This means that more tokens were available for trading during the period, which potentially added to selling pressure.

While that is no longer the case, the latest data shows that the XRP supply index has jumped by 3.9 points in just 53 days, moving from supply abundance to severe supply tightness in just about two months.

This typically suggests that XRP is being aggressively moved out of exchanges despite its prolonged price weakness, potentially driving a rebound in the demand for XRP, which could eventually trigger a price recovery.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recognition honors Jacobsen's invention of reciprocal deposits and nearly 25 years of innovation, helping banks compete and serve their communities.
  • Sources indicate that ARLINGTON, Va., Nov.
  • The recognition celebrates Jacobsen's contributions to helping community and regional banks attract and retain deposits, allowing them to grant access for their customers to aggregate higher levels of FDIC insurance coverage and enabling them to better serve their communities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recognition honors Jacobsen's invention of reciprocal deposits and nearly 25 years of innovation, helping banks compete and serve their communities.

Sources indicate that ARLINGTON, Va., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mark P. Jacobsen, Cofounder and CEO of IntraFi, was named an EY Entrepreneur Of The YearÂ® 2026 National Award winner in the Financial Services category, recognizing his pioneering contributions to the banking industry and his leadership in building the nation's largest reciprocal deposit network.

The recognition celebrates Jacobsen's contributions to helping community and regional banks attract and retain deposits, allowing them to grant access for their customers to aggregate higher levels of FDIC insurance coverage and enabling them to better serve their communities.

In a recent development, nearly 25 years ago, Jacobsen recognized a challenge facing community banks and their customers. Businesses and municipalities often needed to maintain deposits exceeding traditional FDIC insurance limits, while smaller banks struggled to compete with larger institutions for those relationships.

Recent findings suggest that jacobsen "conceived the idea of reciprocal deposits," wrote EY in its recognition. "IntraFi created an entirely upcoming banking product.".

Sources indicate that reciprocal deposit services allow community banks to place uninsured deposits through a deposit placement network in increments below FDIC insurance limits and receive a matching amount of insured deposits in return. This allows small businesses, public funds and nonprofits to obtain higher levels of aggregate FDIC insurance. This benefits both the bank and its customers, allowing depositors to have a single relationship with their preferred institution while the bank can use the full amount of the deposit to fuel economic growth.

It has been revealed that "Jacobsen brought the idea to life by combining a regulator's understanding of the financial system and an entrepreneur's instinct to challenge conventional thinking, plus the resolve to see the challenge through," said EY, noting Jacobsen's former role as the chief of staff of two federal banking regulators. "He earned a dozen patents and worked with all the federal banking agencies as well as state and local governments, prompting more than 40 state laws to enable the use of reciprocal deposits.".

Industry observers note that today, IntraFi operates the nation's largest reciprocal deposit network, connecting more than 3,000 financial institutions, the vast majority of which are community banks. IntraFi's scale, sophisticated infrastructure, and proven reliability distinguish it from other providers, with established systems that have supported banks through multiple financial crises and periods of market stress.

"Any recognition belongs solely to the employees of IntraFi and the thousands of banks that have put their faith in us," mentioned Jacobsen. "We built this network bank by bank with a commitment to do things the right way, not relying on marketing puffery or short-lived promises. And we remain committed to constant innovation. Whether it's helping community banks compete for deposits or exploring how our network could support the next generation of payments, our goal remains the same: giving banks the tools they need to better serve their customers.".

IntraFi's unmatched network scale and proven operational reliability reinforces its position as a trusted partner to banks of all sizes.

The EY Entrepreneur Of The Year program recognizes entrepreneurs whose innovation, leadership, and vision have transformed industries and created lasting economic and community impact.

Sources indicate that intraFi has built the largest financial network of its kind, connecting thousands of financial institutions nationwide. The organization is the nation's leading provider of reciprocal deposit services and a leading provider of overnight and term funding options. IntraFi helps financial institutions manage liquidity, access funding, and provide customers with solutions for keeping large deposits safe.

IntraFi is not an FDIC-insured bank, and deposit insurance covers the failure of an insured bank. A list identifying IntraFi network banks appears at https://www.intrafi.com/network-banks. Certain conditions must be satisfied for "pass-through" FDIC deposit insurance coverage to apply. Use of an IntraFi service is subject to the terms, conditions, and disclosures in the applicable program agreements.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Orchard Robotics, an agtech company using artificial intelligence to help growers monitor crops and make farming decisions, has been acquired by John Deere.
  • The startup has developed a system of cameras mounted on tractors and other equipment that gather images as the machines traverse a farm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 20, 2026 at 7:52 amNovember 20, 2026 at 9:14 am.

Orchard Robotics, an agtech company using artificial intelligence to help growers monitor crops and make farming decisions, has been acquired by John Deere. The deal was revealed Thursday and the terms were not disclosed.

The startup has developed a system of cameras mounted on tractors and other equipment that gather images as the machines traverse a farm. Orchard’s AI analyzes the images to generate data on vines, trees and crops, which is then used to track growth, yield and health.

“This acquisition connects crop-level intelligence with John Deere technology and equipment that can precisely execute the work in the field,” Tim Marquis, John Deere’s director of farm systems innovation, said in a statement.

That includes helping farmers target treatments and make better-timed decisions about thinning, spraying and harvesting.

Orchard was founded by CEO Charlie Wu, a Thiel Fellow who dropped out of Cornell University to launch his business in 2022.

“Over these next few years, our goal is to bring the power of Orchard’s industry-leading technology and AI Farming capabilities to every farmer out there,” Wu noted in a LinkedIn post. “This is only the beginning of a long and awesome journey ahead.”.

According to recent reports, the startup is based in San Francisco and has an office in Seattle. Wu splits his time between the two cities and was a finalist for Young Entrepreneur of the Year at the 2026 GeekWire Awards.

Industry observers note that orchard has raised more than $25 million from investors, including a $22 million Series A round confirmed in September 2025. The startup has 45 employees, according to PitchBook.

The Pacific Northwest is home to numerous agtech startups. That includes other companies that collect and analyze data, such as Loftus Labs and innov8.ag, as well as IUNU and Koidra, which are focused on greenhouse crops. Businesses tackling field operations include weed destroyers Carbon Robotics and Aigen; rock-removing TerraClear; and irrigation startups FarmHQ and Verdi.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin (BTC), the world’s largest cryptocurrency, is flashing a major, ‘scary’ technical signal that was absent even during its last major crashes in February and June 2026.

The flagship coin has crashed to a fresh 4.5-month low amid persistent institutional outflows totaling billions from cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

It has been revealed that $BTC hasn't formed a higher high for 16 consecutive days now. This didn't even happen during the Feb 2026 and June 2026 crashes. https://t.co/I6IPmdueEc.

In a recent development, bitcoin has failed to form a higher high for the past 16 days. This is a very long stretch, one that was absent during Bitcoin’s February and June crashes.

According to recent reports, A higher high, in the context of technical analysis, is formed when an asset’s price reaches a newly introduced high point above its previous swing high. The absence of higher highs signals that buyers are having a hard time taking back control of the market.

The latest Bitcoin price action adds further to concerns surrounding the future of the flagship cryptocurrency.

Earlier today, BTC crashed to $61,225, its lowest price point in around four and a half months.

Bitcoin's failure to create higher highs despite several attempts to recover shows that selling pressure remains quite high.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, this technical pattern of 16 days without a higher high does not necessarily spell more pain for Bitcoin. If the cryptocurrency can decisively push above recent resistance zones, it may be a sign that buyers are starting to make a comeback.

Bitcoin is facing persistent withdrawals of huge amounts of money from U.S.-based spot Bitcoin ETFs.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) witnessed its biggest-ever daily net outflow on Nov. 19.

It has been revealed that the crypto fund suffered a whopping $541.1 million in net withdrawals on the day. At the same time, total net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs amounted to around $582.3 million across the entire market.

It has been revealed that more alarmingly, the fresh wave of withdrawals brings cumulative net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs to around $3.47 billion so far this November.

The ETFs have seen negative net flows on 12 of the first 14 trading days of the month.

The transaction, which closed July 1, 2026, makes 25 eligible employees beneficial owners of the literacy publishing and education technology company at no cost to them. DiGilio will continue to lead the company as CEO.

In a recent development, "After a cancer diagnosis made me think hard about what happens to this organization without me, I realized I wanted the people who built it to own its future," said DiGilio. "So I sold, not to a private equity firm, but to our teachers, curriculum writers, warehouse staff, and customer support team. When the owners are the people doing the work, children stay first in every decision.".

"I've always cared deeply about the work we do, but knowing I now have a personal stake in the organization's future makes it even more meaningful," stated Tricia Martineck, digital accounts manager at Laprea. "It's exciting to be part of something that's growing while making a difference in the lives of children.".

Industry observers note that diGilio taught second grade for 23 years before founding Laprea. The firm now serves more than 800 school districts in all 50 states, employs about 50 people, and was named to the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies in 2025 and 2026. DiGilio was also named to the 2026 Inc. Female Founders 500.

According to recent reports, laprea's flagship line, Developing Decoders, includes more than 1,200 fiction and nonfiction decodable books written to align with popular phonics programs. The company also publishes Teacher in a Backpack take-home literacy kits, hands-on phonics tools, and professional development for teachers, and has donated more than 256,000 books to children in the United States, Kenya, and Zimbabwe.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 13:50 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Recent findings suggest that australia-based Myriota Pty. Ltd., a global satellite platform for the industrial internet of things, today confirmed it has raised $40 million in the first portion of its Series C to launch next-generation satellites and accelerate customer adoption across international markets.

Main Sequence Ventures, Hostplus and Australia’s National Reconstruction Fund Corporation co-led the round. Funds SA joined as a new investor. The round raised the company’s total funding to more than $107.5 million, and is expected to close in early 2027.

Founded in 2015, Myriota’s platform makes satellite connectivity commercially viable for large-scale industrial IoT, using the same core technology to track mining equipment and trailers to also monitor fuel tanks, livestock water supplies and off-grid solar.

It has been revealed that the company’s platform combines satellite connectivity, low-power devices, field installation tools and fleet management software to support existing infrastructure. The objective is to provide access to communication tools that connect what is in place with turnkey service, so a company can connect devices, machines and smart sensors no matter how remote they are.

“We’re at the beginning of a fundamental shift in industrial IoT,” Chief Executive Ben Cade stated. “Industries increasingly rely on data from the field to make decisions about their operations, assets and resources, and as AI moves into the physical world, that data becomes even more essential.”.

The company expanded its platform over the past 12 months with the launch of HyperPulse, a global 5G non-terrestrial network, or NTN, and terrestrial service, and AssetHawk, a rugged, long-life asset tracker designed to make it economical to track industrial objects.

According to recent reports, alongside the expansion, it also grew into latest verticals such as industrial fuels. It monitors and tracks fuel deployments across North America and Latin America, with EMEA and Asia Pacific to follow.

It has been revealed that myriota competes in a sector led by established operators such as Iridium Communications Inc., Orbcomm Inc. and Viasat Inc., alongside a growing field of providers pursuing cheaper, standards-based connections for industrial sensors and trackers.

The firm mentioned it intends to use the funds to expand its space infrastructure, including developing and launching its next-generation satellites.

Industry observers note that bitcoin road back toward $80,000 may have a new catalyst after news from US regulators. CFTC has opened another door for crypto inside traditional financial markets. CFTC notes regulated derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses can count Bitcoin toward certain financial requirements. But what does this mean?

According to recent reports, the guidance could help firms hold onto their Bitcoin instead of selling it to satisfy reserve requirements. It undoubtedly changes how regulated institutions can use BTC. This news comes as Bitcoin looks for reasons to reverse its recent weakness.

According to recent reports, CFTC ALLOWS EXCHANGES COUNT BITCOIN FOR OPERATING COSTS.🚨 THIS IS HUGE !!!👉 Bitcoin enters clearinghouse reserves. pic.twitter.com/vP0NyuwLU3.

Released yesterday, it allows eligible firms to use Bitcoin, Ether, and qualifying payment stablecoins toward resources covering 12 months of operating costs. BTC and ETH face a minimum 20% haircut, while qualifying stablecoins face just 2%.

Bitcoin still has plenty of ground to recover, but can this news reverse the current bleeding trajectory?

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026.

Under the guidance, regulated derivatives exchanges, swap facilities, and clearinghouses can include certain crypto holdings in their financial-resource calculations. A firm holding $1 million in Bitcoin could count $800,000 after the minimum haircut.

The allowance comes with a catch: crypto cannot satisfy the separate requirement for cash or highly liquid securities. Major exchanges and clearinghouses must still cover at least six months of operating costs with qualifying liquid assets.

Recent findings suggest that still, the change removes a barrier for firms already holding crypto. They can now put some of those assets to work toward regulatory requirements instead of relying entirely on traditional holdings. That could make Bitcoin a little more practical for firms operating inside the US derivatives market.

It has been revealed that bitcoin needs more than regulatory progress to climb 33%. The market has suffered heavy losses, and BTC remains well below its October 2025 peak above $126,000. A move toward $80,000 would require buyers to regain control and reverse the recent downtrend.

The CFTC guidance won’t force institutions to buy BTC, but it gives regulated firms a reason to accommodate the asset. The timing is notable, with Bitcoin struggling around $60,000 and investors looking for signs that institutional demand could return.

According to recent reports, A move toward $80,000 remains a tall order from here. But Bitcoin and its expanding role in regulated markets are giving us a fresh view to point to, even as the price and chart still need to confirm the recovery.

Tech Report: StepSecurity, led by two Microsoft vets, raises $20M to defend developers’ tools from hackers

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (879 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 20, 2026 at 8:28 amNovember 20, 2026 at 8:34 am.
  • StepSecurity’s co-founders spent more than two decades combined at Microsoft.
  • Their old employer is not the only one with this problem.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 20, 2026 at 8:28 amNovember 20, 2026 at 8:34 am.

StepSecurity’s co-founders spent more than two decades combined at Microsoft. This week, as their startup announced a fresh round of funding, its researchers were also investigating a hacked Microsoft software package.

Their old employer is not the only one with this problem.

In a recent development, stepSecurity, a Seattle-area cybersecurity startup, raised a $20 million Series A round led by Elephant, with participation from existing investors Runtime Ventures, Inner Loop Capital and SaaS Ventures. The tech giant has now raised $23 million, including a $3 million seed round in 2024. Axios Pro first reported the latest round.

The startup protects the systems used to build software: developers’ laptops, code repositories, package downloads and CI/CD pipelines, the automated systems that assemble and ship code.

Sources indicate that the problem is that attackers increasingly slip malicious code into open-source software that developers download. That code can do damage as soon as it runs on a developer’s laptop or build system, stealing the passwords and keys that unlock other systems.

“A supply chain attack used to take a skilled team,” CEO Varun Sharma wrote in a blog post announcing the funding. “Now one person can vibe code it.”.

Recent findings suggest that sharma spent about 15 years at Microsoft, where he led a team in Azure Security focused on making security easier for developers. CTO Ashish Kurmi spent nearly eight years at Microsoft before leading cloud security at Uber and infrastructure security at Plaid.

The two met at Microsoft and started StepSecurity in 2021, after working through the fallout from the SolarWinds and Codecov supply chain attacks at their respective employers.

A busy week: The Microsoft package, agent-framework, is the Python version of Microsoft’s open-source toolkit for building AI agents.

It has been revealed that it gets roughly 190,000 downloads a month. Two malicious versions published on Nov. 17 to PyPI, the main public repository for Python software, included code designed to steal cloud and CI/CD credentials as soon as Python started up, SecurityWeek reported. PyPI quarantined both versions, and a Microsoft maintainer remarked an investigation was underway.

That’s one entry in a long list. StepSecurity’s announcement also cites the $6.3 billion Binance breach in October, which the FBI attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Binance has mentioned the attack started with a compromised employee laptop.

According to recent reports, it also points to a tampered copy of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension that sat in Cursor’s extension marketplace for about 11 hours last month. Cursor mentioned up to 5,000 consumers may have received the malicious version.

StepSecurity says it documented 56 confirmed compromises of trusted software components between August 2025 and August 2026, and roughly one every three days from March 2026 through the August report.

How it works: StepSecurity got its start with its own tool, Harden-Runner, which is free for open-source projects. It watches automated builds on GitHub and flags anything unexpected in the processes they run, the network connections they make or the files they change.

More than 20,000 open-source projects use it, the manufacturer says, up from about 3,000 at the time of the seed round. Unusual behavior spotted in those public builds has helped StepSecurity catch attacks early, the company says, including the March 2025 compromise of tj-actions, a widely used add-on for GitHub’s build automation.

StepSecurity’s paid products also protect developers’ laptops and check code repositories. Its Secure Registry service screens software packages before a company’s builds download them from public sources such as npm, the main public repository for JavaScript packages. It blocks versions known to be compromised and holds brand-new releases for a waiting period, giving researchers time to catch malicious ones before anyone installs them.

Recent findings suggest that along with the funding, StepSecurity is making Secure Registry free for public GitHub projects that use Harden-Runner and run their builds on GitHub’s servers. The free version defaults to a two-day waiting period and supports JavaScript packages, with Python, Java, Ruby and Rust planned.

Recent findings suggest that stepSecurity has plenty of competition. Socket, a San Francisco startup that screens open-source packages for malicious code, raised $60 million at a $1 billion valuation in May. Sonatype, JFrog and Endor Labs also sell tools that can block risky packages before they’re installed.

It has been revealed that growth spurt: StepSecurity indicates its annual recurring revenue grew fivefold in 2024, fivefold again in 2025 and more than fivefold so far this year. It didn’t disclose dollar figures.

Named customers include Circle, Dexcom, Kong, Mercari, Chainguard and XBOW.

In a recent development, the company has 27 employees, up from four, including the founders, at the time of the seed round. Sharma is based in Sammamish and Kurmi in Kirkland, and the rest of the remote-first team is spread across the U.S., Canada and India.

What’s next: StepSecurity aims to extend its protections to agent sandboxes, the isolated environments where AI agents run code. Its argument is that anyone who asks an AI agent for a spreadsheet may be downloading and running open-source packages.

The tech giant notes it also plans to double its team over the next 12 months, mostly in security research, engineering and sales and marketing.

Shiba Inu’s layer-2 network, Shibarium, is experiencing a major slowdown as daily network activity has fallen to three-digit figures (fewer than 1,000 transactions), hitting lows not seen in months.

It has been revealed that shibarium processed 546 transactions, according to Shibariumscan data, marking a slower period for the layer-2 network after activity spiked to a high of 6,370 on October 31, 2026. Transaction activity declined afterward, and the decline intensified amid the sell-off that hit the market in recent weeks.

The latest figures suggest that fewer transactions are taking place across Shibarium compared with periods of stronger activity. The key question now is whether Shibarium can regain momentum in the coming weeks.

Meanwhile, development continues behind the scenes for the Shiba Inu layer-2 network, as long-time Shiba Inu community member and developer Mazrael revealed a massive batch of contracts deployed on Puppynet, Shibarium's testnet.

But in the meantime, Shibarium’s fall to three-digit activity levels is a major slowdown that SHIB holders and ecosystem watchers will be watching closely.

Shiba Inu's on-chain holders increased as the number of wallets holding SHIB hit 1,700,930 on November 19, 2026.

According to the latest figures shared by Etherscan SHIB, an X account dedicated to providing updates on the SHIB ecosystem, the cryptocurrency added 236 new on-chain holders in a single day, taking its total past the 1.7 million milestone.

The month of November has also seen consistent growth, with SHIB adding 4,520 holders since the start of the month. The broader 2026 trend is even more pronounced, with the number of holders of the token increasing by 152,300 since the beginning of the year.

While Shiba Inu's latest milestone seems remarkable, Mazrael suggested that the Shib ecosystem, including Shibarium, might have more holders than indicated, with 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on the BNB Chain.

Recent findings suggest that "Shibarium has more holders than those you listed, though. But yeah. Well, there are also 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on BNB. But that's not actually CCIP SHIB; it is a peg," Mazrael wrote.

NEAR Protocol (NEAR) fell 11.41% on Nov. 20 and traded at $2.84, according to TradingView data. In early October, the token was trading near $6, and it has lost about half of its value since then.

Sources indicate that over the same period, the volume of NEAR Intents went up. "NEAR went from $6 to $3 in about a month. funny thing is, NEAR Intents is doing more volume now than it did in october," NEAR ecosystem contributor Evgeny Haenko wrote on X on Nov. 20.

According to Haenko, NEAR Intents averaged around $129 million in daily volume in October, and in November it was processing around $134 million a day. "The price got cut in half, the business didn't slow down at all. hard for me to be bearish here," he wrote.

NEAR Intents lets users swap assets across more than 30 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and XRP. The service is built into wallets such as Ledger, Trust Wallet and Brave. Over the past year, its trading volume grew 7.1 times to $39.5 billion.

It has been revealed that NEAR Intents has collected about $63 million in fees in total, and the network keeps about 29% of that amount. Fees on the NEAR Intents interface, payments from B2B partners and the spread on better-than-market trades accounted for 16.3%, 9.9% and 2.8% of the fees, respectively. Over the last 30 days, the protocol earned about $1.8 million, compared with $2.2 million in October.

In a recent development, since February 2026, the protocol has used NEAR Intents revenue to buy NEAR on the market. More than 1.84 million NEAR have gone to the buyback wallet so far, and that is 41.6% of all distributed onchain revenue. Base transaction fees on the network are burned in full.

According to recent reports, in early November, the NEAR community also voted to cut the maximum annual issuance from 2.5% to 1.6% over two years. The proposal, HSP-029, went through House of Stake, NEAR's governance initiative, and Haenko is one of its participants.

On Sept. 29, Bitwise launched the first U.S. spot NEAR ETF on NYSE Arca under the ticker NRR. Two days later, on Oct. 1, NEAR Intents paused its services after an exploit that cost about $3.8 million, and the team promised to compensate users in full. The exploiter later returned the funds. "The funds from the $3.8M NEAR Intents hack were sent back in full," NEAR Intents general manager Alex Shevchenko mentioned at the time.

  • Industry observers note that in a memo to staff on Friday, Jason Henderson, who is president of M365 Core, described it as the most customer-impacting incident Exchange Online has ever had, according to Reuters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft $MSFT has declared a "Code Red" to rework how it averts and handles serious breakdowns of its services, after a 24-hour outage revealed flaws in its engineering systems and crisis response, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters.

The Nov. 12-13 outage disrupted Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 products. It struck governments across Australia, Japan and the U.S., caused delays for trading firms and interrupted airline communications.

Industry observers note that in a memo to staff on Friday, Jason Henderson, who is president of M365 Core, described it as the most customer-impacting incident Exchange Online has ever had, according to Reuters. "Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team," he wrote. He noted no earlier disruption had left so many customers without email for such a stretch.

It has been revealed that amanda Silver, a corporate vice president overseeing M365 Core and Work IQ, described in a different Monday memo reviewed by Reuters how engineers had operated amid a "fog of war." Responders sent upwards of 11,000 messages spread over 11 Teams chats. Because diagnostic data was held in disjointed internal tracking systems, they had trouble keeping a single coherent view of the theories being tested and the decisions made, she stated.

Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, mentioned during a Code Red review that the component involved had undergone "roughly ten years' worth of acceptable failures," according to Silver's memo.

It has been revealed that silver laid out five workstreams that address shedding load, dividing traffic by geography and speeding up recovery. Microsoft has set itself a goal of fixing any future incident across the globe in under an hour. It intends to put AI agents to work so engineers can interpret data on system health more rapidly.

Henderson will meet daily with the Substrate leadership team, which supervises the engineering organization in charge of the services that underpin Microsoft 365, according to Reuters. He will also hold weekly reviews.

Industry observers note that henderson wrote in an earlier memo this month, which Reuters also reviewed, that M365 Core services were too slow to roll out urgent patches globally. In one recent incident, an urgent production fix needed five to six days to fully spread across the globe, he wrote. He wants the most urgent security problems fixed and safely rolled out worldwide within an hour of being detected, he noted, but Microsoft has not yet reached that mark.

"Our work doesn't end when service is restored," a Microsoft spokesperson told Reuters. "Our teams keep working around the clock to promptly implement any lessons learned, and our leadership makes sure this is our top priority.".

Industry observers note that microsoft traced the outage to a software bug that had sat undetected in its data centers since July, detailing the cause in a preliminary report to customers on Nov. 15. The report stated load testing missed the flaw because labs favored weaker hardware with fewer cores. CEO Satya Nadella apologized publicly, and Microsoft said neither cyber activity nor AI agents had a role in the failure.

#87572. How the surge in AI-discovered bugs is straining Microsoft security and threatening tech stability

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1875 w)
